items.text: A group of Iranians gathered on Tuesday, 14 Mehr, in front of the UK Prime Minister's office. They protested against the execution of their compatriots by the Islamic Republic. The gathering was in support of those sentenced to death in Iran.

Abdolnaser Hemmati, the governor of the Central Bank, said that the American officials' promise of the collapse of Iran's economy will not come true. He understands the economic pressures on the people and the government is trying to reduce problems during the economic war.

A number of Farda Motors customers gathered on Tuesday, October 6, in front of the judiciary in Semnan province. They protested the judicial process of the company's case. They also criticized the imposition of an unfair agreement.

Workers of North Drilling Company reported delays in payment of their wages and claims. Workers of Mohammadan CNG station have not been paid for five months, and workers of Maroon Oil and Gas Industrial Complex No. 6 are facing three months of unpaid wages and non-payment of insurance premiums.

The Spanish football team defeated Croatia 2-1 in their fourth match in the UEFA Nations League. Mikel Merino scored both goals for Spain, while Ivan Perisic scored for Croatia. This victory brought Spain's total points to 12.

Omid Memarian reported the arrest of another suspect in the suspicious activities around the Fairford base. He examined the possibility of the detainees' connection to a foreign government. If the role of the Islamic Republic is proven, the national security of Britain and Europe will be directly involved.

The England football team defeated the Czech Republic 3-0 in their fourth match in the UEFA Nations League. The goals were scored by Vladimir Coufal and Harry Kane (twice). England reached 9 points and ranked second in Group 3 with this victory.

Ghassan Ashour, a Middle East analyst, reported the advance of Yemeni government forces in Bab al-Mandab and Dhubab. He attributed these advances to increased coalition attacks led by Saudi Arabia and air superiority. Ashour stated that the fall of Sanaa would not mean the end of the Houthis, and neither side can completely defeat the other.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, in a speech in Maryland, called the Islamic Republic the 'evil and bully of the Middle East' but said Iran's government is 'not so much of a bully anymore.' He emphasized that the job must be finished and the only question is which way to do it; the good way or the not-so-good way, and you will find out soon.

Donald Trump stated that the US operation against the Islamic Republic is progressing very well and the path to end the conflict will soon be determined. He said Iran's air and naval forces have been destroyed and its defense systems damaged. Trump also claimed that the Strait of Hormuz is under US naval control.

Donald Trump stated that the US Navy has imposed an effective and impenetrable blockade against Iran. He said the Strait of Hormuz is now under US Navy control and no ship can pass through the blockade. Trump also emphasized that the US does not need Iranian oil, but other countries depend on it.

British police arrested the seventh suspect in connection with a suspected plot to attack an airbase hosting American bombers. The suspect is a 22-year-old British national in London. After receiving intelligence reports, a fleet of B-1 bombers was withdrawn from the RAF Fairford base.

After the execution of Alireza Raeisi, his father was transferred blindfolded and without being informed of the exact burial location. The burial took place in a desert area near Isfahan, and the family remains unaware of the exact grave site. Security officials have stated that the burial location will be announced later.

A group of political activists and Iranians residing in Germany gathered on Tuesday, October 6, in Hanover and Hamburg. They protested the execution of Alireza Sepahi and Alireza Raeisi and demanded the release of political prisoners. The participants also expressed their support for Reza Pahlavi.

JD Vance, the US Vice President, stated that Iran must significantly reduce its nuclear enrichment capacity. He emphasized that the US is ready for an agreement but demands specific nuclear concessions. Vance also pointed to uncertainty in Iran's decision-making structure.

The CEO of the Thalassemia Association announced that each thalassemia patient now spends over 100 million tomans monthly on treatment. The cost of some medicines has increased more than 600 times after the removal of preferential currency. Additionally, pharmacies' claims have not been paid for over 10 months, and insurance companies are delayed in covering the increased drug prices.

A number of scholarship applicants and those seeking status change to contractual employment gathered in front of the Ministry of Science. They protested the prolonged process of issuing employment codes and positions. They demanded resolution of their employment status issues.

Financial Times reported that due to increased attacks by the Islamic Republic on ships, oil tanker captains receive a monthly salary of $100,000 and a $50,000 bonus per trip for passing through the Strait of Hormuz. Ship owners pay a 'danger allowance' to encourage sailors, and ordinary crew members receive four to six times their usual wages. Most ships pass through the strait at night with GPS signals turned off.

Ali Akbar Rashad announced that the Spiritual Health field has been designed as an official and scientific discipline. This field has been launched at the Imam Reza seminary. The level of this field is equivalent to a PhD.

A shopkeeper stated that the price increase of the new chip batch is not limited to 70-gram packages. Other similar products have also become more expensive. This was reported in a video received by Iran International.

Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, said that the Islamic Republic has missed multiple opportunities for a nuclear agreement with the US. He emphasized that Iran will never acquire nuclear weapons and its military capability has diminished. He also stated that the Strait of Hormuz is open and Iran's economy is in a very dire situation.

Iran International audiences report worsening living conditions for workers, teachers, and nurses. Issues include temporary contracts, partial salary payments, and insurance cuts. Rising dollar prices and inflation have reduced people's purchasing power.

Turkey plans to send more air defense forces and equipment to Saudi Arabia in the coming weeks following intensified Houthi attacks. Ankara's focus is on countering drones and providing intelligence support. Turkey does not intend to intervene directly in the Yemen war.

The Qatari government has opposed a direct flight for Esteghlal team to Doha. Esteghlal must first travel to Najaf in Iraq and then take another flight to Doha. The match between Al-Gharafa and Esteghlal will be held on October 12.

Three years ago on October 7, Hamas attacked Israel, resulting in about 1,200 deaths and 251 hostages. The Nova music festival in a non-residential area was one of the first places targeted. This event was reported by Babak Es-haqi from Iran International.

A student stated that Azad University of Rudehen criticizes female students' dress code instead of improving academic quality. The university charges high tuition fees. The student's voice was reprocessed with artificial intelligence for security.
Following a shooting by military forces in Bandar Abbas, a fuel transporter vehicle overturned and caught fire. In this incident, a disabled fuel transporter lost his life.
Workers at the Iran-Break Rasht factory have gone on strike due to unpaid wages and insurance. The protest began yesterday and continues today. They have gathered in front of the factory entrance.

Clashes between Yemeni government forces and Houthis around the Bab al-Mandab Strait have intensified. Mohammadjavad Akbarin highlighted the importance of this area for maritime security and the global supply chain. He also stated that the Islamic Republic has destabilized countries and positioned the Houthis against Yemen's legitimate government.
The head of the Masal Environmental Protection Department announced the issuance of a fine for a person accused of animal abuse in this county.

Etemad newspaper reported that housing expenses account for 40% of the monthly expenditures of the urban middle class and 48% for the urban poor. Arzoo Karimi stated that renting is no longer only a problem in large cities, and rent increases in these cities are also significant. This report was published on World Tenants' Day.
